claims.text: The initial system is an elemental Cr coating deposited on a zirconium-alloy cladding substrate.
Heating the Cr-coated substrate at approximately 500°C in an oxygen-rich environment for approximately 2 hours will form a Cr2O3 layer.
The resulting Cr2O3 layer will be uniform, dense, and ultrathin.
The Cr2O3 surface film will span the thickness of the original Cr coating.
Cr2O3 is chemically inert under the proposed service conditions.
The preformed Cr2O3 layer has sufficiently low ionic diffusivity to function as a diffusion barrier.
A Cr2O3 layer on the outer surface of the coating will inhibit Cr–Zr atomic interdiffusion at the coating–substrate interface.
The barrier will minimize migration of Cr into the Zr substrate during high-temperature exposure.
Suppressing Cr migration will maintain coating integrity and corrosion protection.
Untreated Cr-coated zirconium alloy undergoes pronounced Cr–Zr interdiffusion that causes coating degradation at high temperature.
Cr coatings can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
Pre-oxidized samples will exhibit significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than untreated Cr-coated samples.
Pre-oxidation will improve coating longevity relative to the untreated baseline.
The pre-oxidized coating will sustain corrosion protection in subcritical water at approximately 320°C.
The pre-oxidized coating will sustain protection in high-temperature steam up to approximately 1100°C.
Subcritical water at approximately 320°C represents the normal-operation boundary.
Steam exposure up to approximately 1100°C represents the accident-relevant boundary.
The long-term stability, cyclic-load durability, mechanical-damage resistance, growth kinetics, and spallation resistance of the proposed Cr2O3 layer remain uncertain.
A controlled comparison of pre-oxidized and untreated samples after 60 days in approximately 320°C water followed by approximately 1100°C steam can discriminate the hypothesis.
Failure to reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion, or scale spallation accompanied by similar or greater oxidation, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes formation of a Cr2O3 surface layer, while the structural mediator says that this surface film spans the entire thickness of the original Cr coating, and the main hypothesis says the elemental coating is transformed into Cr2O3. These imply materially different geometries: an external scale, a through-thickness converted coating, or complete replacement of elemental Cr.

If Cr2O3 is only an outer surface film, it is not located at the buried Cr–Zr interface where interdiffusion occurs. The hypothesis does not explain how that surface film blocks Cr and Zr transport at the opposite side of the remaining Cr coating.
